title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1986 'Analysis situs' axiomatics of an 'atelier' (workshop). It consists of a poset of 'lieux' (places) (M, ≤), a second relation ≪ (roughly 'X is a small or interior piece of Y'; its exact meaning is fixed on earlier pages), and a symmetric relation ≭ between lieux. I read ≭ as 'in compatible disposition': the two lieux are in good relative position, so that they can be treated together. There is also a set 𝓕 of 'figures' F, with associated sets F̃ ⊂ M of lieux, intersections F∩G, and an empty figure ∅_𝓕. The previous page reduced the structure F̃ to M, in the finite-type case, as closed subsets of M whose elements are pairwise ≭.

On this page Grothendieck turns to 'disposition-compatibility' axioms. He says they are optional for an atelier and will have many mutual implications with the axioms on lieux. He wants to restate them in terms of disjointness.

Definition: F ∥ G (F and G disjoint) iff F ≭ G and F∩G = ∅_𝓕. He notes this depends only on ≤. Equivalently, F ∥ G iff X ∥ Y for all X ∈ F̃ and Y ∈ G̃. Here, for lieux, X ∥_M Y means X ≭ Y and {X,Y} has no lower bound in (M,≤): there is no Z with Z ≤ X and Z ≤ Y. In a NB he remarks that the stronger statement 'no Z with Z ≪ X, Z ≪ Y' should follow from the previous axioms together with what comes below.

He then drafts AtDC 1, the 'axiom of special ateliers'. A margin note says an atelier will be called special if it satisfies these axioms. The axiom: let X, Y ∈ M and K = X∩Y = sup of the Z ∈ X̃∩Ỹ. Suppose that for all X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y with X' ∥ K and Y' ∥ K we have X' ∥ Y'. Then X ≭ Y. A bracketed NB says this is in fact 'iff', cf. the Corollary.

Corollary, for figures F, G with K = F∩G: F ≭ G iff every pair of small pieces X ≪ F, Y ≪ G that both avoid K are themselves disjoint.

In words, two figures are in compatible position exactly when they 'touch only along their intersection': pieces of F and G away from F∩G never meet. This is a cleanness or transversality-type criterion, reducing compatibility to disjointness away from the common part.

The whole block is struck through. On the next page it is reworked into 'Propriété 1', which says that for F ≭ G with L = F∩G, compatibility of sub-figures can be tested after 'removing' L, and into AtDD1. There Grothendieck notes that one direction of the related criterion is false in the 'linear' case (cf. At 11, GF 68).
errors: The equivalence F∥G ⇔ (∀X∈F̃, Y∈G̃, X∥Y) silently uses that ≭ between figures is equivalent to pairwise ≭ between their lieux. This is consistent with the previous page's description of F̃_tf, but only shown there for figures of finite type; the general (infinite antifiltration) case is not justified.

The 'iff' in the Corollary (marked 'NB et alors seulement... cf Cor') is asserted without proof. The next page shows Grothendieck himself found that a closely related converse fails in the linear case, which is presumably why the AtDC1 block was crossed out and reformulated.
When K = ∅_𝓕, the hypothesis X'∥K is vacuous and the axiom reduces to: (all X'≪X, Y'≪Y disjoint) ⇒ X≭Y. Whether this is intended or degenerate is not discussed.

ideas.what: Disjointness of figures defined as compatible position plus empty intersection, and characterized lieu-wise as compatibility plus no common lower bound in (M,≤)
ideas.modern_name: disjointness of closed sets or subcomplexes in a poset of strata/cells (no common face)

ideas.what: Axiom of 'special ateliers' (AtDC1): two figures are in compatible disposition iff small pieces of each that avoid their intersection are disjoint
ideas.modern_name: a cleanness / 'meeting only along the intersection' criterion for mutual tameness; loosely akin to compatibility of stratifications or of definable sets in o-minimal geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct counterpart; tame-topology axiomatics are due to van den Dries, Shiota and others in o-minimal form
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of 'topologie modérée' is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6; the atelier axiomatics are unpublished.

ideas.what: Programme of making disposition-compatibility axioms 'optional' layers on an atelier, with mutual implications with axioms on lieux
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology / abstract stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (programmatically, Esquisse); formal theories by o-minimalists
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches the desire for an axiomatic tame topology, but not these axioms.

missed.claim: Grothendieck attempts an axiom characterizing when two figures are in compatible position purely by disjointness of their pieces away from the intersection. He abandons it (struck out) and reformulates it on the next page after noticing a failure in the linear case. Whether some correct version holds in o-minimal or PL settings, and what class of 'special ateliers' it defines, was not pursued.
missed.quote: Alors F ≭ G ssi ∀X,Y∈M, X≪F, Y≪G, X∥K, Y∥K ⇒ X∥Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with known results on compatible stratifications or cell decompositions of pairs of definable sets. The value lies more in documenting Grothendieck's unpublished atelier axiomatics than in a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of unpublished, partly crossed-out axiomatics for Grothendieck's 'ateliers'. The disjointness notion is routine. The abandoned 'special atelier' axiom is a mildly interesting unpublished detail of his tame-topology programme, but it is tentative, flagged by Grothendieck himself as problematic, and contains no finished result.
transcription_corrections: NB line: reads closer to '(NB Il résulte des axiomes précédents que ∄Z avec Z≪X, Z≪Y, [?] résultera d'axiomes ... et de ce qu'on vérifie ci-dessous...)', i.e. 'Il résulte' rather than 'Je n'ai'.
In AtDC1, the bracket reads '[NB et alors seulement... cf Cor]' ('et alors seulement' = 'and only then', i.e. iff), not 'et dans seulement'.
In the Corollary, the circled word is 'ssi'.
Left margin: roughly 'Un atelier sera dit spécial s'il satisfait les conditions ci-dessous / les axiomes ci-dessous...'; the word 'spécial' is attached to the heading 'Axiome des ateliers spéciaux'.

Line 3: the insertion above the line seems to be 'avoir l'air de' attached to 'énoncés sur les lieux'. The phrase 'pour en parler en jeu[?] disjonction' likely reads 'pour en parler en termes de disjonction'.
